name: TMP112AIDRLR
title: TMP112 and TMP112D: ±0.5 °C, low-power digital temperature sensors with a two-wire bus, in SOT563 and X2SON
summary: The TMP112 family are local temperature sensors that convert their own die temperature to a 12-bit two's-complement word (0.0625 °C per LSB, 13 bits in extended mode for readings past 128 °C) and report it on an I2C, SMBus and two-wire compatible bus up to 2.85 MHz. They run from 1.4 V to 3.6 V, draw about 3.2 µA at one conversion per second and 0.15 µA shut down, and have an open-drain ALERT output with programmable limits, fault queue, polarity and comparator or interrupt behaviour. The TMP112A, B, D and N in SOT563 differ in accuracy grade; the TMP112D and TMP112D0 to D3 also come in an 0.8 mm X2SON whose centre pad is either the address pin or ALERT. TMP112AIDRLR is the TMP112A (±0.5 °C max from 0 °C to 65 °C at 3.3 V) in SOT563 on a 4000-piece reel.

circuits.title: Typical connections, SOT563-6
circuits.description: One sensor in SOT563 on a two-wire bus run by a host controller. Three 5 kΩ resistors pull SCL, ALERT and SDA up to the 1.4 V to 3.6 V supply, a 0.01 µF capacitor bypasses V+, and ADD0 is grounded, which gives the part bus address 48h.
notes: SCL, SDA and ALERT each need a pull-up resistor.

circuits.title: Typical connections, X2SON-5
circuits.description: Both X2SON variants sharing one I2C bus. U1 is an alert variant (TMP112D0, D1, D2 or D3, address fixed by part number) whose ALERT output goes to the controller; U2 is the address variant TMP112D with ADD0 grounded, giving 40h. Three 5 kΩ resistors pull ALERT, SDA and SCL up to the 1.4 V to 3.6 V supply, and one 0.01 µF capacitor bypasses the supply.

circuits.title: Supply RC filter for noise reduction (SOT563-6 shown)
circuits.description: The sensor fed through a series resistor with a capacitor to ground at its V+ pin, an RC filter that cuts the noise the part puts back on the supply. R(F) is at most 5 kΩ and C(F) at least 10 nF. ADD0 is grounded; SCL, SDA and ALERT run out to the bus.

operation.text: Every member has the same 12-bit converter (0.0625 °C per LSB), 1.4 V to 3.6 V supply and two-wire interface; they differ in accuracy grade and package. TMP112A is graded for 3.3 V and TMP112B for 1.8 V (±0.5 °C max over 0 °C to 65 °C at that supply), TMP112N is a ±1 °C part, and the TMP112Dx parts hold ±0.5 °C over –25 °C to 85 °C from 1.5 V up. TMP112A/B/D/N come in the 1.6 mm × 1.6 mm SOT563; TMP112D and TMP112D0 to D3 also come in the 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm X2SON. Production units are tested against NIST-traceable references. TMP112-Q1 and TMP112D-Q1 are automotive versions.

The sensing element is the die itself. Heat reaches it mostly through the package leads, whose metal has lower thermal resistance than the mould compound. The TMP102 is a lower-accuracy, pin-compatible part in the same package.

Each conversion overwrites a read-only register of 12 bits (EM = 0) or 13 bits (EM = 1), left-justified in two bytes, most significant byte first; reading only the first byte is allowed. Negative values are two's complement. Bit D0 of the second byte reads 0 in normal mode and 1 in extended mode, and unused bits read 0. Until the first conversion after power-up or reset finishes, the register reads 0 °C.

The part is a target only, never driving SCL. SDA and SCL are open-drain with spike filters and Schmitt-trigger inputs. It handles the fast, fast-plus and high-speed protocols, with SCL from 1 kHz up to 400 kHz, 1 MHz and 2.85 MHz respectively; data go MSB first. The address pin selects one of four addresses, so four parts can share a bus.

Every write begins, after the address byte with R/W low, with a pointer byte whose two low bits pick the register; P2 to P7 must be 0. A read returns the register last pointed to, so to change it the host writes only the pointer, then issues a repeated START and the address with R/W high. The pointer is kept, so repeated reads of one register need no new pointer. Registers move as two bytes, most significant first; a host ends a read with a not-acknowledge or a START/STOP.

In interrupt mode (TM = 1) ALERT may serve as the SMBus alert line; the alert status is set whether or not the package has the ALERT pin. When the host sends the alert response address (0001 1001), an alerting part acknowledges and returns its own address, whose LSB is 1 if the temperature went above T(HIGH) and 0 if it went below T(LOW). Several parts answering arbitrate; the lowest address wins and clears its alert, the others stay active.

The part acknowledges the general-call address (0000 000 with the eighth bit 0). A second byte of 0000 0110 resets every internal register to its power-up value. The general-address acquire command is not supported.

Above 400 kHz the host first sends the Hs-mode controller code 0000 1xxx after a START. The part does not acknowledge it but switches its SDA and SCL filters to high-speed operation, up to 2.85 MHz, and stays there until the next STOP, when it returns to fast-mode filtering.
If SCL is held low for 30 ms (typ) between a START and a STOP, the interface resets and releases SDA, then waits for a new START. An SCL rate of at least 1 kHz keeps the timeout from tripping.

Continuous conversion is the default. Each conversion takes about 10 ms, after which the converter powers down until the next one is due at the rate set by CR1 and CR0 (0.25, 1, 4 or 8 Hz; 4 Hz by default). A conversion starts right after power-up or a general-call reset, so the first result is ready after about 10 ms. Supply current is 55 µA typ while converting and 2.6 µA typ between conversions (27 °C), in both packages.
EM = 0 uses 12-bit data in the temperature and limit registers, the format of the TMP75. EM = 1 switches all three to 13 bits so temperatures above 128 °C can be represented.

With the part shut down, writing 1 to OS starts one conversion; OS reads 0 while it runs and 1 when it is done, and the part goes back to shutdown. A conversion takes about 10 ms and a read under 20 µs, so more than 80 conversions per second are possible this way.
SD = 1 shuts down everything but the serial interface once the conversion in progress finishes, bringing current to typically under 0.15 µA in either package. SD = 0 returns to continuous conversion.

T(HIGH) and T(LOW) use the temperature register's format and are compared with every result. In comparator mode (TM = 0) ALERT and the status flag go active once the temperature has reached or passed T(HIGH) on the set count of successive conversions, and return inactive after it has stayed under T(LOW) for that same count. In interrupt mode (TM = 1) ALERT goes active at T(HIGH) and stays so until any register is read, the part answers the SMBus alert response, or it is shut down; after that it goes active again only when the temperature falls below T(LOW), and is cleared the same way, and the cycle repeats. A general-call reset also clears ALERT and returns the part to comparator mode. Power-up limits are T(HIGH) = 80 °C and T(LOW) = 75 °C.

operation.topic: Polarity, fault queue, resolution and AL bit
operation.text: POL = 0 (default) makes ALERT and its flag active low; POL = 1 makes them active high. F1 and F0 set how many consecutive out-of-limit results (1, 2, 4 or 6) are needed before an alert, to reject noise. R1 and R0 are read-only and read 11, meaning 12-bit resolution. AL is a read-only comparator status: with POL = 0 it reads 1 until the temperature has reached T(HIGH) for the set fault count, then 0 until it has fallen below T(LOW) for the same count; POL inverts it and TM does not affect it. The configuration register is written byte by byte, and its first byte matches the TMP75 and TMP275 configuration register.

SCL, SDA and ALERT need pull-up resistors; 5 kΩ is the recommended value, and other values are allowed provided no pin sinks more than 3 mA. SCL and SDA may be pulled up to a rail equal to or above V+. A 0.01 µF bypass capacitor sits as close to V+ and GND as possible, with more decoupling for noisy or high-impedance supplies. An optional RC filter in the supply (R(F) ≤ 5 kΩ, C(F) ≥ 10 nF) further reduces the small noise the part injects. Keeping SDA and ALERT pull-up current low avoids self-heating that lowers accuracy. The part works across 1.4 V to 3.6 V and is optimised for 3.3 V.

The part measures the temperature of the board where it sits, so it is placed close to the heat source with good thermal coupling, for instance a ground plane running to the source. For air or surface measurement the package and leads are isolated from the surrounding air, and a thermally conductive adhesive helps for surface readings. Plunged from 25 °C into a 100 °C oil bath on a 0.5 in × 0.5 in two-layer board, both packages reach 63 % of the step in about 1.2 s; the time constant depends on board size.

The X2SON centre pad is ADD0 on the address variant and ALERT on the alert variants. For ADD0 it can be tied by a same-layer trace to one of the four edge pads. For ALERT there are two ways out: a 0.1 mm (4 mil) trace between pads 1 and 5 or 2 and 4, where the gap between pads is at most 0.26 mm (10.2 mil), leaving 0.08 mm (3.15 mil) clearance; or a via in the centre pad, under 0.305 mm (13.78 mil) diameter to stay inside the pad, with a 0.1 mm (4 mil) minimum drill, which calls for a 0.125 mm (5 mil) annular ring. Which way to go depends on what the PCB fabricator can hold. The board carries a thermal pad under the package, and the package is soldered to it.
